title: Scheduled quiesce window and deferred artifact sync for Private/VPC upgrades
creator: Marisol Vega
description: Define requirements and acceptance criteria for a deploy-time quiesce (scheduled pause) and a deferred artifact synchronization mechanism for Private/VPC deployments. This is aimed at customers who operate in restricted egress environments or air-gapped sites and need predictable, short maintenance windows with deterministic rollback guarantees.
context: Customers running Redwood Private in isolated VPCs have two recurring issues during platform upgrades: (1) unbounded upgrade duration when nodes continuously accept new traffic or background syncs, and (2) inability to pull artifactory/manifest updates during restricted egress windows. Engineering has proposed an operator-assisted quiesce mode that: gracefully drains new inference sessions, pauses background artifact replication, and defers non-critical syncs to a controlled post-upgrade window. This ticket formalizes the product contract and acceptance criteria.
scope: In scope: operator-level APIs to schedule a quiesce window; UI/CLI controls for initiating quiesce and deferred sync; upgrade orchestration integration (canary stage respects quiesce); image/artifact validation and signed-blob enforcement during deferred sync; audit/logging hooks and observability for quiesce events. Out of scope: full redesign of KV-cache replication logic, cross-region WAN optimization, and support for physical media distribution (separate project).
non_goals: Not enabling automatic customer-side workload draining beyond Redwood-managed inference processes; not providing a generic cron-based file-sync engine for arbitrary customer artifacts.
constraints: Must operate with zero or strictly controlled egress (mirrors or signed artifact staging required). Quiesce windows must be configurable per-cluster and support emergency abort. All behavior must be reversible with operator-initiated rollback within a published SLA.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Cluster-level quiesce API exists (operator CRD + console action) that schedules a maintenance window with start/end timestamps and reason metadata.
AC-2: During quiesce, new inference sessions are rejected with HTTP 503 + Retry-After header; in-flight sessions are allowed to complete within a configurable drain timeout (default 60s).

AC-3: Background artifact syncs (images/manifests/helms) are transitioned into deferred state and will not initiate outbound requests during the quiesce window unless explicitly allowed by an allowlist entry.
AC-4: Deferred syncs can be executed post-upgrade in a controlled 'deferred sync' phase; operator exposes an idempotent resume endpoint and progress is tracked in audit logs.
AC-5: For air-gapped customers, the operator supports staged artifact apply where customer-provided signed manifests are accepted; unsigned artifacts are rejected and surfaced in the console.
AC-6: Canary and canary-fallback logic respects quiesce windows: canary nodes are only promoted if quiesce is not active or if canary explicitly opted-in to run under quiesce constraints.
AC-7: KMS key rotation flow documented: if KMS rotation is required during upgrade, operator enters prepared state and can defer rotation until after operator-verified artifact validation completes.
AC-8: All quiesce lifecycle events (schedule, start, abort, resume) emit structured events to telemetry and are queryable in the console timeline with user and request IDs.

AC-9: Rollback during or immediately after quiesce must complete within an operator-defined SLA (default 10 minutes for control-plane rollback actions) and leave cluster in a consistent and observable state.
AC-10: Upgrade runbook containing quiesce playbook, rollback steps, and customer communication templates is checked into Confluence and linked from the console.
rollout_plan: Step 1: Feature flag gated rollout to internal staging clusters for 2 weeks with simulated restricted-egress tests.
Step 2: Small closed beta with 3 consenting customers across different egress configurations (mirror, proxy, true-airgap).
Step 3: Expand to broader private deploy customers with opt-in in console; monitor for anomalous rollback rates for 7 days.
Step 4: Default enablement for new private clusters behind an onboarding toggle and documentation refresh.
Step 5: Post-rollout review + bake period (30d) to decide on GA enablement and SLAs.
test_plan: TP-1: Automated DRY-RUN test that simulates quiesce scheduling and validates drift between requested and actual start/end timestamps.
TP-2: E2E test: start quiesce while generating 100 concurrent short-lived inference requests; assert 503 for new sessions after drain-time and completion of in-flight requests.
TP-3: Airgap acceptance test: customer-supplied signed manifest applied during deferred sync phase; operator validates signature and transitions artifact to active state without egress.
TP-4: Failure injection: abort quiesce mid-window and verify operator resumes deferred syncs only after a manual resume action.
TP-5: Rollback SLA tests: induce a failed upgrade during quiesce and measure time-to-rollback and cluster consistency checks.
risk_assessments: R1: Customers with long-running sessions could experience failed work if drain timeout misconfigured — mitigated by conservative defaults and clear console warnings.
R2: Incorrect signature validation logic could block deferred syncs — mitigate with exhaustive compliance tests and an emergency bypass for signed-off artifacts.
R3: Telemetry blind spots during quiesce may hide failures — include redundant logging to control-plane persistent store.
notes: Design to be compatible with existing operator lifecycle hooks and not require additional cluster-level privileged network egress during quiesce. PM to coordinate with Solutions Engineering for customer-facing docs and support runbooks.
